explain.say: In 1808 Napoleon's armies seized Spain and put his brother Joseph on the throne. Across the Atlantic, people in Mexico City, Caracas and Buenos Aires asked a dangerous question: if our king is gone, who rules us now? Within about sixteen years almost all of Spain's mainland American empire was independent. Look at the timeline.

explain.say: See the causes. Criollos, people of Spanish descent born in the Americas, resented that Spanish-born officials got the top jobs. Bourbon reforms had raised taxes and tightened control from Madrid. And the United States, France and Haiti showed that old empires could fall. Which cause was the spark, and which were the dry wood?

explain.say: Mexico went first and differently. On 16 September 1810 a priest, Miguel Hidalgo, called his parishioners to rise. Tens of thousands of Indigenous and mixed-race peasants followed, which frightened the elites. Hidalgo was executed in 1811, and Mexico won independence in 1821 through a conservative deal. Why would wealthy criollos fear a peasant army?

explain.say: Now the map shows two great campaigns. Simón Bolívar fought from Caracas to Bogotá, winning at Boyacá in 1819. José de San Martín led an army over the Andes from Argentina into Chile in 1817, then sailed to Lima. They met in 1822, and Spain's last big army surrendered at Ayacucho in Peru in 1824. Brazil took a different road, an empire under Prince Pedro.

Who gained? See the comparison. Criollo elites took power, but slavery lasted into the 1850s in many states and until 1888 in Brazil, and many Indigenous communities lost land. Bolívar's dream of a united Gran Colombia broke up by 1831. Great job. Exam tip: separate political independence from social revolution in your answer.

faq.q: Why did Latin America become independent?
faq.a: Napoleon's seizure of Spain in 1808 created a crisis of who held legitimate power. Criollo elites, angry at exclusion and Bourbon taxes and inspired by the American, French and Haitian revolutions, formed their own governments, and wars by Bolívar, San Martín and others defeated Spanish forces.
asks: What did Napoleon have to do with it?

faq.a: A Venezuelan criollo leader who led independence wars in Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia, which is named after him. He hoped for a united Gran Colombia, but it split apart by 1831.
People of Spanish descent born in the Americas. Many were rich landowners and merchants but were kept out of the highest offices, which mostly went to peninsulares, people born in Spain.
asks: What is the difference between criollos and peninsulares?

faq.a: A Mexican priest who, on 16 September 1810, called on his parishioners in Dolores to rise against colonial rule, the Grito de Dolores. His mass movement was defeated and he was executed in 1811, but 16 September is Mexico's independence day.
asks: What was the Grito de Dolores?

faq.q: Who gained from Latin American independence?
faq.a: Mainly criollo elites, who took political power and opened trade. Slavery was abolished only gradually, Indigenous communities often lost land, and many new states faced decades of civil war and strongman rule.
asks: Did independence end slavery in Latin America?

facts: Miguel Hidalgo issued the Grito de Dolores on 16 September 1810.
The Battle of Ayacucho in December 1824 ended Spain's main resistance in South America.
Brazil declared independence from Portugal in 1822 under Pedro I.
